cls: Anti-osteoporotic agent - dual-action bone modulator (osteoanabolic and anti-resorptive)
pharm: Divalent strontium salt of ranelic acid that simultaneously stimulates osteoblast-mediated bone formation and inhibits osteoclast-mediated bone resorption, increasing bone mineral density and reducing fracture risk in osteoporosis.
quick: 2 g oral granules (suspended in water) once daily at bedtime
Take >=2 h away from food, milk, calcium and other medicines; bedtime preferred
Contraindicated; not for women of childbearing potential
Avoid; do not use while breastfeeding
Contraindicated if CrCl <30 mL/min; not recommended in severe impairment
No specific adjustment; limited data, use with caution
No direct interaction; minimise as part of bone-health/CV risk advice
Cardiovascular/ischaemic risk at baseline and every 6-12 months; skin reactions (DRESS); BMD
summary: Strontium ranelate (Protelos/Osseor/Protaxos, Servier) is an EMA-authorised dual-action anti-osteoporosis agent given as 2 g oral granules once daily, taken at bedtime at least 2 hours away from food, milk and calcium. It both increases bone formation and decreases bone resorption, reducing vertebral and hip fracture risk. Use is RESTRICTED to severe osteoporosis in postmenopausal women and adult men at high fracture risk for whom other osteoporosis treatments are unsuitable, because the drug carries an increased risk of myocardial infarction and venous thromboembolism and can cause life-threatening severe cutaneous reactions including DRESS (Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms), Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis. It is contraindicated in patients with current or past ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease, cerebrovascular disease, venous thromboembolism, or uncontrolled hypertension. The marketing authorisation holder withdrew Protelos from the EU market in 2017. NOT FDA-approved - this entry is based on the EMA Summary of Product Characteristics (SmPC) and BNF.
indications: Treatment of severe osteoporosis in postmenopausal women at high risk of fracture, to reduce the risk of vertebral and hip fractures, where treatment with other medicinal products approved for osteoporosis is not possible (e.g. contraindications or intolerance)
Treatment of severe osteoporosis in adult men at increased risk of fracture, where treatment with other approved osteoporosis medicines is not possible

dosage.d: 2 g once daily (one sachet of granules suspended in a glass of water)
dosage.n: Take >=2 h after the evening meal; restricted to patients for whom other agents are unsuitable

dosage.d: 2 g once daily (one sachet of granules suspended in water)
dosage.n: Same dosing and restrictions as in women; ensure adequate calcium and vitamin D intake separately

dosage.d: 2 g once daily; no dose adjustment for age
dosage.n: Efficacy and safety established across the studied age range; reassess CV risk regularly

admin: Empty the sachet of granules into a glass, add water, stir to form a suspension and drink immediately (drink promptly after preparing)
Take at bedtime, preferably at least 2 hours after eating
Separate from food, milk and dairy, calcium-containing products and antacids by at least 2 hours (they reduce absorption)
Ensure adequate calcium and vitamin D intake if dietary intake is inadequate, but take these supplements at a different time of day
Before starting and periodically, assess cardiovascular and thromboembolic risk; do not start if CV/ischaemic contraindications are present
moa: Strontium ranelate has a dual mechanism that rebalances bone turnover in favour of bone formation. In vitro and in vivo it increases bone formation by stimulating osteoblast precursor replication and collagen/non-collagenous protein synthesis, while simultaneously reducing bone resorption by inhibiting osteoclast differentiation and resorbing activity. The divalent strontium cation is taken up by bone, partly substituting for calcium in the hydroxyapatite crystal lattice and adsorbing onto crystal surfaces. The net effect is increased bone mineral density (part of the apparent BMD gain on DXA reflects strontium's higher atomic weight) and a reduction in vertebral and hip fracture risk.

absolute: Current or past ischaemic heart disease (e.g. angina, myocardial infarction)
Current or previous venous thromboembolism (DVT, pulmonary embolism), including past history
Temporary or permanent immobilisation (e.g. post-surgical recovery, prolonged bed rest) due to VTE risk
Hypersensitivity to strontium ranelate or any excipient
relative: Risk factors for venous thromboembolism (assess need to continue in patients >80 years at risk of VTE)
Risk factors for cardiovascular/ischaemic disease (hypertension, hyperlipidaemia, diabetes, smoking) - weigh against benefit
Phenylketonuria - the granule formulation contains aspartame (a source of phenylalanine)
Severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min) - not recommended
monitor: Cardiovascular and ischaemic risk before initiation and at regular intervals (generally every 6-12 months)
Signs of severe skin reactions, especially in the first weeks of treatment (rash, fever, lymphadenopathy, eosinophilia - DRESS)
Symptoms of venous thromboembolism (leg swelling/pain, breathlessness, chest pain)

preg: Contraindicated in pregnancy. Strontium ranelate should not be used by women of childbearing potential unless effective contraception is used. Animal data showed reversible bone effects in offspring; there are no adequate human data. If pregnancy occurs during treatment, stop the drug.
lact: Contraindicated during breastfeeding. Strontium is excreted in animal milk, and use during lactation is not recommended; do not breastfeed while taking strontium ranelate.
renal: Contraindicated/not recommended in severe renal impairment (creatinine clearance <30 mL/min) because of lack of efficacy and safety data. No dose adjustment is required for mild to moderate impairment (CrCl 30-70 mL/min). Periodically assess renal function in at-risk patients.
hepatic: No specific dose adjustment is provided. Strontium ranelate is not metabolised by the liver and pharmacokinetics are not expected to be altered, but data in hepatic impairment are limited - use with caution.

major: Quinolone antibiotics (e.g. ciprofloxacin) - strontium chelates and markedly reduces their absorption; separate dosing or interrupt strontium
Tetracycline antibiotics (e.g. doxycycline) - reduced antibiotic absorption; separate dosing or interrupt strontium while on the antibiotic
moderate: Oral calcium supplements and other di/trivalent cation products - reduce strontium absorption; separate by >=2 hours
Antacids (aluminium/magnesium hydroxide) - reduce strontium absorption; take >=2 hours apart
Concomitant agents that increase VTE/CV risk - additive risk given the drug's vascular profile
minor: No clinically significant cytochrome P450-mediated interactions (strontium is not metabolised by CYP enzymes)
interactions.food: Food, milk and dairy products and calcium reduce bioavailability by about 60-70%; take at bedtime at least 2 hours after eating and away from calcium.
interactions.alcohol: No specific pharmacokinetic interaction with alcohol; moderate intake as part of general bone-health and cardiovascular risk reduction.
interactions.diagnostics: Strontium interferes with colorimetric methods for blood and urine calcium determination - use inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectrometry or atomic absorption spectrometry instead. Strontium accumulation in bone increases DXA-measured BMD beyond the true effect.

serious: Venous thromboembolism - deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism
DRESS (Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms) - potentially fatal hypersensitivity
Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis
rare: Bone marrow disturbances (e.g. eosinophilia as part of DRESS)
emergency: Severe skin reaction (DRESS/SJS/TEN): rash with fever, blistering, mucosal involvement, lymphadenopathy - STOP drug immediately and seek urgent care; do not re-challenge
Pulmonary embolism (sudden breathlessness, pleuritic chest pain) or DVT

monitoring: Cardiovascular and ischaemic risk assessment before starting and at regular intervals (generally every 6-12 months); discontinue if ischaemic heart disease, PAD, cerebrovascular disease or uncontrolled hypertension develops
Watch for severe cutaneous reactions, especially within the first weeks - if DRESS/SJS/TEN suspected, stop permanently
Signs and symptoms of venous thromboembolism
Bone mineral density / fracture status to assess treatment response (interpret DXA with awareness of strontium artefact)
Renal function in patients at risk
counsel: Take the granules once a day at bedtime, mixed in a glass of water, at least 2 hours after food and away from milk, calcium tablets and antacids
STOP the medicine and seek urgent medical help if you develop a skin rash - especially with fever, swollen glands or blistering - as this can be a serious, life-threatening reaction

This medicine can increase the risk of heart attack and blood clots; tell your doctor about any heart, circulation or clotting problems, and report chest pain, breathlessness, or a painful swollen leg
Do not use if you are or could become pregnant, or are breastfeeding
Keep your regular check-ups so your heart and circulation risk can be reviewed; continue calcium and vitamin D as advised but at a different time of day
pk: Anti-fracture/BMD effect develops over months of continuous use
Plasma peak ~3-5 hours after a 2 g oral dose
Once-daily dosing maintains effect; strontium retained long-term in bone
Store below 30 C / at controlled room temperature; keep dry
pearls: NOT FDA-approved - this monograph is based on the EMA Summary of Product Characteristics (Protelos/Osseor) and the BNF; it was authorised in the EU, not the US

REGULATORY STATUS: EU use was progressively restricted (PRAC/CHMP 2013-2014) to severe osteoporosis at high fracture risk with no CV/ischaemic contraindications; the marketing authorisation holder (Servier) withdrew Protelos/Osseor from the EU market in 2017

CARDIOVASCULAR SIGNAL: pooled trials showed an increased risk of myocardial infarction (~1.7% vs 1.1% with placebo); contraindicated in ischaemic heart disease, PAD, cerebrovascular disease, VTE and uncontrolled hypertension
DRESS / severe skin reactions can be fatal - greatest risk in the first few weeks; stop permanently at the first sign of rash with systemic features and never re-challenge

Take at bedtime and keep >=2 h from food, milk and calcium - dairy and calcium cut absorption by ~60-70%; strontium also inflates DXA-measured BMD and interferes with colorimetric serum/urine calcium assays
missed: If a dose is missed, simply skip it and take the next dose at the usual bedtime - do not take a double dose to make up. Because absorption requires an empty stomach and separation from calcium, do not take a missed bedtime dose with food the next morning.
overdose: Strontium ranelate has low acute toxicity; in studies single doses up to 11 g were well tolerated. There is no specific antidote. In overdose, induce vomiting if recent and give milk or antacids (calcium-containing products) to reduce strontium absorption, then provide supportive care. Strontium can be removed slowly; monitor and treat symptomatically.
